_**Lagaan: Once Upon a Time in India**_, or simply _**Lagaan**_, (transl.Land Tax) is a 2001 Indian [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi")-language [epic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_film "Epic film")[period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_film "Period film")[sports drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_drama "Sports drama") film[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-5) written and directed by [Ashutosh Gowariker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashutosh_Gowariker "Ashutosh Gowariker"). The film was produced by [Aamir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan"), who stars alongside debutant [Gracy Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gracy_Singh "Gracy Singh") and [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_people "British people") actors [Rachel Shelley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Shelley "Rachel Shelley") and [Paul Blackthorne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Blackthorne "Paul Blackthorne"). Set in 1893, during the late [Victorian period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_era "Victorian era") of [British colonial rule in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj"), the film follows the inhabitants of a village in [Central India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India_Agency "Central India Agency"), who, burdened by high taxes and several years of drought, are challenged by an arrogant [British Indian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Indian_Army "British Indian Army") officer to a game of [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") as a wager to avoid paying the taxes they owe. The villagers face the arduous task of learning a game that is alien to them and playing for victory.

Produced on a budget of ₹25 crore (US$5.3 million), _Lagaan_ was the [most expensive Indian film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_Indian_films "List of most expensive Indian films") at the time of its release.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-6) It faced multiple challenges during production: Khan was initially sceptical about starring in a sports film, and later, prospective producers called for budget cuts and script modifications. Eventually, the film would become the maiden project of Aamir Khan Productions, and mark Khan's foray into film production. Gowariker was inspired by aspects of the sports drama _[Naya Daur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naya\_Daur\_(1957\_film) "Naya Daur (1957 film)")_ (1957) in developing the film. The language featured in the film was based on [Awadhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awadhi_language "Awadhi language"), but was diluted with standard Hindi for modern audiences. Principal photography took place in villages near [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj"). [Nitin Chandrakant Desai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitin_Chandrakant_Desai "Nitin Chandrakant Desai") served as art director, while [Bhanu Athaiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhanu_Athaiya "Bhanu Athaiya") was the costume designer. The original soundtrack was composed by [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman"), with lyrics written by [Javed Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar "Javed Akhtar").

_Lagaan_ was theatrically released in India on 15 June 2001, clashing with _[Gadar: Ek Prem Katha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gadar:\_Ek\_Prem\_Katha "Gadar: Ek Prem Katha")_. It received widespread critical acclaim for Gowariker's direction, Khan's performance, dialogues, soundtrack, and the film's [anti-imperialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-imperialist "Anti-imperialist") stance. With earnings of ₹65.97 crore (US$13.98 million) during its initial release, the film was the third [highest-grossing Hindi film of 2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Hindi_films_of_2001 "List of Hindi films of 2001"). _Lagaan_ was screened at numerous international film festivals and garnered multiple accolades. It was the third, and as of 2025 the last, Indian film to be nominated for the [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film") after _[Mother India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother\_India "Mother India")_ (1957) and _[Salaam Bombay!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salaam\_Bombay! "Salaam Bombay!")_ (1988). _Lagaan_ became the most-awarded film at the [47th Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/47th_Filmfare_Awards "47th Filmfare Awards") with eight wins, including [Best Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Film "Filmfare Award for Best Film"), [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Director "Filmfare Award for Best Director") for Gowariker and [Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor") for Khan.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-7) At the [49th National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/49th_National_Film_Awards "49th National Film Awards"), the film won eight awards, including [Best Popular Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Popular_Film_Providing_Wholesome_Entertainment "National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-8).

The film is considered to be one of the greatest films ever made in [Indian cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cinema "Indian cinema") of the 2000s.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-10)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In 1893, the farmers of the village of [Champaner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaner "Champaner"), located within the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj")[Central India Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India_Agency "Central India Agency"), endure an oppressive colonial administration. Despite a devastating drought and a failed harvest, British officials demand the regular [_lagaan_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_value_tax "Land value tax") (land tax). Led by a resilient young farmer named Bhuvan, the villagers appeal to their local ruler, Raja Puran Singh, for a tax waiver. Their petition is intercepted by the arrogant and sadistic regiment commander, Captain Andrew Russell. Russell proposes a high-stakes wager: the villagers will play a game of [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") against his elite British officers. If the villagers win, their lagaan will be completely canceled for three consecutive years; if they lose, they must pay triple the standard tax, an ultimatum that would guarantee their starvation. Bhuvan boldly accepts the challenge, and the match is scheduled three months later.

Bhuvan initially faces intense skepticism and isolation, as the terrified villagers refuse to believe they can master an unfamiliar British sport. Slowly, he recruits a diverse group of eleven players, including a [low-caste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caste_system_in_India "Caste system in India")[untouchable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Untouchability "Untouchability") named Kachra, whose [spin-bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_bowling "Spin bowling") abilities prove lethal. Meanwhile, Russell’s sister, Elizabeth, arrives from [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"). Horrified by her brother's cruelty and secretly infatuated with Bhuvan, she decides to covertly coach the village team on the rules and strategies of the game. However, a jealous villager named Lakha, who covets Gauri—the village medic's daughter currently courted by Bhuvan—agrees to act as an insider informant and saboteur for Captain Russell. As the match approaches, Russell is severely reprimanded by his superiors for wagering the government treasury, and is warned that he will be court-martialed and forced to pay the taxes himself if the British lose.

The three-day match commences outside the British cantonment. On the first day, the British team bats first and builds a formidable score, heavily aided by the villagers' technical inexperience and Lakha’s deliberate sabotage on the field. That night, Elizabeth witnesses Lakha conferring with Russell and exposes the betrayal to the villagers. When the angry locals attack Lakha, Bhuvan intervenes, offering him a chance at redemption. Conscience-stricken, Lakha plays exceptionally well on the second day, executing critical catches that trigger a sudden British collapse, capping their innings at a daunting 322 runs. Champaner's batting response starts disastrously, losing their top batsmen rapidly to aggressive British bowling.

On the third and final day, Bhuvan anchors the collapsing innings, staging a heroic resistance alongside injured teammates. The tension peaks in the final over of the game, with the villagers requiring five runs off the final delivery to achieve victory. Russell delivers the ball, and Bhuvan strikes it high into the sky. Russell catches the ball and celebrates prematurely, but the umpire signals a no-ball as Russell had crossed the boundary line while catching it, granting Champaner a six. The villagers win the match against all odds, just as dark storm clouds burst to end the long drought. Amidst the euphoric celebrations, Elizabeth watches Bhuvan and Gauri embrace, realizing her love will remain unrequited.

In the aftermath, Elizabeth bids a poignant farewell to the grateful villagers and returns to England, where she spends the rest of her life unmarried, carrying her memories of Bhuvan. The narrator reveals that the humiliated British administration immediately transfers Russell to [Central Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Africa "Central Africa") and disbands the entire provincial regiment to cover up the embarrassment. Bhuvan and Gauri are married in a grand celebration blessed by Raja Puran Singh. Although Champaner's historic triumph effectively saved the entire province from ruin, the miraculous event ultimately slipped entirely through the cracks of documented history.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Development")]

_Lagaan_ was inspired by _[Naya Daur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naya\_Daur\_(1957\_film) "Naya Daur (1957 film)")_ (1957), a [sports drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_drama "Sports drama") film directed by [B. R. Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._R._Chopra "B. R. Chopra"), written by [Akhtar Mirza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akhtar_Mirza "Akhtar Mirza") and Kamil Rashid, and starring [Dilip Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar"), [Vyjayanthimala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyjayanthimala "Vyjayanthimala") and [Ajit Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajit_Khan "Ajit Khan").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-12)

Director Gowariker has stated that it was almost impossible to make _Lagaan_. He went to Khan, who agreed to participate after hearing the detailed script. Khan had initially rejected the idea of a "sporty" film, but was "himself in tears" upon hearing the full dialogued script.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-location-13) Even after securing Khan, Gowariker had trouble finding a producer. Producers who showed interest in the script wanted budget cuts as well as script modifications. Eventually, Khan agreed to Gowariker's suggestion that he would produce the film.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-14) Khan corroborated this by saying that the faith he had in Gowariker, the story and script of the film,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw1-15) and the opportunity of starting his own production company inspired him to produce _Lagaan_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw3-16) He also said that by being a producer himself, he was able to give greater creative freedom to Gowariker. He cited an example:

> "If the director tells the producer that he wants 50 camels, the latter will probably say, 'Why not 25? Can't you manage with 25 camels?' Whereas, if he is telling me the same thing... I will not waste time asking him questions because I am also creatively aware why he needs them."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw2-17)

[Jhamu Sughand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhamu_Sughand "Jhamu Sughand") co-produced the film because he liked the emotional and patriotic story.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-toi2008-19)_Lagaan_ was made on a [then-unprecedented budget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_Indian_films "List of most expensive Indian films") of [₹](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_rupee "Indian rupee")250 million (US$5.32 million), the highest for an Indian film of the time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-budget-4)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-20)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casting")]

Gowariker first thought of [Shah Rukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan"), [Bobby Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Deol "Bobby Deol"), [Hrithik Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrithik_Roshan "Hrithik Roshan") and [Abhishek Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhishek_Bachchan "Abhishek Bachchan") for the role of Bhuvan. After Bachchan chose to enter cinema with [J. P. Dutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._P._Dutta "J. P. Dutta")'s _[Refugee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee\_(2000\_film) "Refugee (2000 film)")_ (2000), Khan was approached with the idea.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-21)

Several actresses had express interest to act in the female lead role in the film, but Khan needed someone who matched the description of the character given in the script. After considering [Rani Mukerji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rani_Mukerji "Rani Mukerji") who did not have dates to accommodate the film, [Sonali Bendre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonali_Bendre "Sonali Bendre"), [Nandita Das](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandita_Das "Nandita Das"), [Shamita Shetty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shamita_Shetty "Shamita Shetty") and [Ameesha Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ameesha_Patel "Ameesha Patel") were approached for the role,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-gracy-22) Gowariker selected Singh for the female lead because he was convinced that she was a good actress and dancer and resembled actress [Vyjayanthimala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyjayanthimala "Vyjayanthimala"). Singh, a newcomer, devoted all her time to the film.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw2-17) Since the script also demanded a British cast, Gowariker and Khan hired Danielle Roffe as one of the [casting directors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casting_(performing_arts) "Casting (performing arts)").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-23) After Danielle and Gowariker screen-tested many, Shelley and Blackthorne were chosen for the prime roles. Overall, the film cast 15 foreign actors.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-24)

[Raghubir Yadav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raghubir_Yadav "Raghubir Yadav") played the role of the legendary [Haji Nasruddin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasreddin "Nasreddin") in the teleplay _Mullah Nasiruddin_ and has given many memorable performances such as _[Mungerilal Ke Haseen Sapne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mungerilal\_Ke\_Haseen\_Sapne "Mungerilal Ke Haseen Sapne")_. Yadav was selected for the role of Bhura, a poultry farmer, based on his performance in _[Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth\_(1998\_film) "Earth (1998 film)")_ (1998). He had undergone an [appendectomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendectomy "Appendectomy") during the filming schedule and returned to complete some of his scenes.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-25)[Rajesh Vivek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Vivek "Rajesh Vivek"), who played the fortune teller Guran, was spotted by Gowariker in the film _[Junoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junoon\_(1978\_film) "Junoon (1978 film)")_ (1978). His liking for cricket helped him in his role.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-guran_intw-26)[Raj Zutshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajendranath_Zutshi "Rajendranath Zutshi")'s friendship with Khan and association in several films brought him the role of Ismail the potter after auditions.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-ismail_intw-27)[Pradeep Rawat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pradeep_Rawat_(actor) "Pradeep Rawat (actor)")'s association with Khan in _[Sarfarosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarfarosh\_(1999\_film) "Sarfarosh (1999 film)")_ (1999) brought him the role of Deva, a [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh") ex-[sepoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sepoy "Sepoy"), which was initially intended for [Mukesh Rishi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukesh_Rishi "Mukesh Rishi"). Rawat claimed that it was the highest ever compensation he received in his career.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-deva_intw-28)[Daya Shankar Pandey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daya_Shankar_Pandey "Daya Shankar Pandey"), who preferred the role of Kachra, was known to Khan and Gowariker through previous films (_[Pehla Nasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pehla\_Nasha "Pehla Nasha")_ (1993), _[Baazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baazi\_(1995\_film) "Baazi (1995 film)")_ (1995) and _[Ghulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghulam\_(film) "Ghulam (film)")_ (1998)). Pandey credited Gowariker for his acting in the film as Goli, saying that Gowariker and he would discuss the required emotions and expressions before shooting.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-29)

[Yashpal Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yashpal_Sharma_(actor) "Yashpal Sharma (actor)") was chosen by Gowariker for the role of Lakha, the woodcutter, after his portrayal in _[Samar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samar\_(1999\_film) "Samar (1999 film)")_ (1999). He said it was a good experience working with Khan and Gowariker during the film.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-30) Amin Hajee earlier worked in a film with Gowariker. The friendly association brought Gowariker to him with the script, which he liked, and thereafter he successfully auditioned for his role of Bagha, a mute drummer. His knowledge of mute people and some assistance from a music band helped him better prepare for his role. Gowariker, who believed that Amin was like [Sylvester Stallone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvester_Stallone "Sylvester Stallone"), would refer to him as Stallone during filming.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-bagha_intw-31)[Aditya Lakhia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aditya_Lakhia "Aditya Lakhia")'s association with Gowariker in _[Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabhi\_Haan\_Kabhi\_Naa "Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa")_ (1993) and _Pehla Nasha_ (1993) brought him the role of Kachra, the untouchable. He read the book _[Everybody Loves a Good Drought](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody\_Loves\_a\_Good\_Drought "Everybody Loves a Good Drought")_ by [P. Sainath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palagummi_Sainath "Palagummi Sainath") to better understand and portray his character.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-kachra_intw-32)

### Pre-production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Pre-production")]

One of the first members to join the production team was [Nitin Chandrakant Desai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitin_Chandrakant_Desai "Nitin Chandrakant Desai"), the art director, with whom Gowariker set out for extensive location hunt throughout India, to find the setting for the fictional town of Champaner, in late 1998. After searching through Rajasthan, Nasik, UP, they zeroed in on an ancient village near [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj"), located in [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat")'s [Kutch district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutch_District "Kutch District"), by May 1999, where the film was primarily shot.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-location-13)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-33)

The script demanded a dry location: an agricultural village where it had not rained in several years. To depict the 1890s era, the crew also required a village which lacked electricity, communication and automobiles.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw1-15) Kutch faced the same problems at that time and hence the village of Kunariya, located a few miles away from Bhuj, was chosen. During the filming of _Lagaan_, it did not rain at all in the region. However, a week after the shoot finished, it rained heavily bringing relief to Bhuj, which had a lean monsoon the previous year.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-gracy-22) The typical old Kutch hamlet was built by the local people four months before the arrival of the crew.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-location-13) The [2001 Gujarat earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake "2001 Gujarat earthquake") devastated this region and displaced many locals. The crew, including the English, contributed to their cause by donating ₹250,000 (equivalent to ₹1,000,000 or US$10,000 in 2023), with further contributions during the year.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-34)

[Avadhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awadhi_language "Awadhi language"), which is a [dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialect "Dialect") of [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi"), is primarily from a region in [Uttar Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uttar_Pradesh "Uttar Pradesh"). It was chosen to give the feel of the language spoken during that era. However, the language was diluted, and modern viewers can understand it.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw2-17) The dialogues, which were a combination of three dialects (Avadhi, [Bhojpuri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhojpuri_language "Bhojpuri language") and [Braj Bhasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braj_Bhasha "Braj Bhasha")) were penned by Hindi writer [K. P. Saxena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._P._Saxena "K. P. Saxena").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-gracy-22)

[Bhanu Athaiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhanu_Athaiya "Bhanu Athaiya"), who won an [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") for her work in _[Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhi\_(film) "Gandhi (film)")_ (1982), was the [costume designer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costume_designer "Costume designer") for the film. With a large number of extras, it was difficult for her to make enough costumes. She spent a lot of time researching to lend authenticity to the characters.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-gracy-22)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Filming")]

The film took approximately a year to plan, which included ten months for production and one month for the development of Khan's character, which the first-time producer found tiring. Khan obtained a crew of about 300 people for six months. Due to the lack of comfortable hotels in Bhuj, he hired a newly constructed apartment and furnished it completely for the crew. Security was set up and a special housekeeping team was brought to take care of the crew's needs.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw3-16) Most of the 19th century tools and equipment depicted in the film were lent to the crew by the local villagers. Initially, they did not want to part with their equipment, but after much coaxing, they gave in. They then travelled to different parts of the country to collect the musical instruments used in that day and era.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw3-16)

During the shooting, Gowariker suffered from a [slipped disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_disc_herniation "Spinal disc herniation") and had to rest for 30 days. During this period, he had his bed next to the monitor and continued with his work.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-35)

The filming schedule spanned the winter and summer, commencing in early January 2000 and finishing in mid-June. This was physically challenging for many, with the temperatures ranging from 0 to 50°C (32 to 122°F).[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-ismail_intw-27)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-bagha_intw-31) The actors had to drink frequently and sit in the shade.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-guran_intw-26)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-deva_intw-28) The schedule was strict. The day began at 6 am, changing into costumes and getting onto the actors' bus, which took them to the sets in Kanuria. The actors, including Khan, all travelled on the same bus. If anyone missed it, it was up to them to reach the sets. One day, Khan was late and missed the actors' bus. That day, his wife Reena, the executive producer, reprimanded him for being late. She told him he had to set an example for the rest of the crew. "If he started coming late, how could she tell the others to come on time?"[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-deva_intw-28) While on the sets, the actors were given call sheets with the day's timetable such as breakfast, hairstyling, make-up, costumes, etc.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-36)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Release")]

Before its worldwide release, Khan kept a promise to screen the film to the locals of [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-37)_Lagaan_ clashed with [Anil Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Sharma_(director) "Anil Sharma (director)")'s _[Gadar: Ek Prem Katha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gadar:\_Ek\_Prem\_Katha "Gadar: Ek Prem Katha")_, starring [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol") and [Ameesha Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ameesha_Patel "Ameesha Patel"), at the box-office.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-39) The film made it to the UK Top 10 after its commercial release.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-40) It was the first Indian film to have a nationwide release in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China")[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-41) and had its dubbed version released in Italy.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Rediff_LIFF-42) With favorable reviews from the French press, _Lagaan_ premiered in Paris on 26 June 2002 and continued to have an unprecedented nine weeks of screening with over 45,000 people watching.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-43) It was released in the United States, Canada, France, Germany, Japan, Malaysia, Hong Kong, South Africa and the Middle East with respective [vernacular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernacular "Vernacular") subtitles.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Rediff_LIFF-42)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-44) The film took a cumulative of $2.5 million at the international box-office and ₹380 million (equivalent to ₹1.5 billion or US$16 million in 2023) at the domestic box-office.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-top-47)

In 2001, _Lagaan_ had a world premiere at the [International Indian Film Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Indian_Film_Academy_Awards "International Indian Film Academy Awards") (IIFA) weekend in [Sun City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_City,_North_West "Sun City, North West"), South Africa.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-48) The [Locarno International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locarno_International_Film_Festival "Locarno International Film Festival") authorities published the rules of cricket before the film was screened to a crowd which reportedly danced to its soundtrack in the aisles.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-49)_Lagaan_ was shown 4 times due to public demand as against the usual norm of showcasing films once at the festival.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Rediff_LIFF-42) It subsequently won the Prix du Public Award at the festival.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-50) After the film's publicity in Locarno, the director, Gowariker said that distributors from Switzerland, Italy, France, Netherlands, North Africa, Finland and Germany were wanting to purchase the distribution rights.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Rediff_LIFF-42) Special screenings were held in Russia, where people were keen to watch the film after its Oscar nomination.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-51)

Apart from these screenings, it was shown at the [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival"),[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-52)[Cairo International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairo_International_Film_Festival "Cairo International Film Festival"),[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-53)[Stockholm International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_International_Film_Festival "Stockholm International Film Festival"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-54)[Helsinki Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki_Film_Festival "Helsinki Film Festival")[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-55) and the [Toronto International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_International_Film_Festival "Toronto International Film Festival").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-56) The film is available on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-57)

### Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Home media")]

There were two releases for the DVD. The first, as a 2-DVD set, was released on 27 May 2002 in limited regions. It contained subtitles in [Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"), English, Hebrew, Hindi, Turkish and several European languages. It is available in 16:9 Anamorphic widescreen, Dolby Digital 5.1 Surround, progressive 24 frame/s, widescreen and NTSC format. It carried an additional fifteen minutes of deleted scenes, filmographies and trailers.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-58)

The second was released as anniversary edition 3-disc DVD box after 6 years of the theatrical release. This also included _Chale Chalo_ which was a documentary on the making of _Lagaan_, a curtain-raiser on the making of the soundtrack, deleted scenes, trailers, along with other collectibles such as 11 collector cards, a collectible _Lagaan_ coin embossed with the character of _Bhuvan_, a 35 mm [CinemaScope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScope "CinemaScope") filmstrip hand-cut from the film's filmstrip were bundled with the film.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-lagaandvd-59) After its release, it became the highest-selling DVD in India, beating _[Sholay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sholay "Sholay")_ (1975).[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-60)_Chale Chalo – The Lunacy of Film Making_, won the [National Film Award for Best Exploration/Adventure Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Exploration/Adventure_Film "National Film Award for Best Exploration/Adventure Film").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-lagaandvd-59)

A comic book, _Lagaan: The Story_, along with 2 colouring books, a mask book and a cricket [board game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_game "Board game") were subsequently released to the commercial market. The comic book, available in English and Hindi, was targeted at children between the ages of 6 and 14. At the book's launch, Aamir Khan said that they were keen to turn the film into a comic strip during the pre-production phase itself.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-62)

In March 2002, a book titled _The Spirit of Lagaan – The Extraordinary Story of the Creators of a Classic_ was published. It covers the making of the film, describing in detail the setbacks and obstacles that the crew faced while developing the film from concept to its release.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-63)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Box office")]

The film initially grossed [₹](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_rupee "Indian rupee")65.97 crore (equivalent to ₹263 crore or US$27 million in 2023) worldwide in 2001. This made it the third [highest-grossing Hindi film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_Hindi_films "List of highest-grossing Hindi films") of 2001, behind _[Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabhi\_Khushi\_Kabhie\_Gham "Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham")_ and _[Gadar: Ek Prem Katha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gadar:\_Ek\_Prem\_Katha "Gadar: Ek Prem Katha")_.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-64)

Domestically, _Lagaan_ grossed ₹55.13 crore (equivalent to ₹219 crore or US$23 million in 2023) in India. Its domestic [net income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net_income "Net income") was ₹34.31 crore, equivalent to ₹187 crore ($25 million) when adjusted for inflation.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-boi-65)

With an overseas gross of ₹10.84 crore[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-top-47) ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")2.2 million) in 2001, it was the year's second [highest-grossing Indian film overseas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_Indian_films "List of highest-grossing Indian films"), preceded only by _Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham_.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-66)_Lagaan_'s overseas gross included [£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_sterling "Pound sterling")600,000 in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), US$910,000 in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"), and US$180,000 in the [Arab states of the Persian Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_states_of_the_Persian_Gulf "Arab states of the Persian Gulf").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-boi-65)

In [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), where the film released on 16 May 2003, it grossed [¥](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renminbi "Renminbi")3 million,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-67) equivalent to ₹ 1.71 crore[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-68) (US$362,500).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-69)

Including the film's China collections, the film's total worldwide gross was ₹67.68 crore (US$14.533 million).[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-70)

### Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

_Lagaan_ was met with critical acclaim. On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 95% of 64 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 7.9/10.The website's consensus reads: "Lagaan is lavish, rousing entertainment in the old-fashioned tradition of Hollywood musicals."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-71)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned the film a score of 84 out of 100, based on 21 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Metacritic-72)

Sudish Kamath of _[The Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hindu "The Hindu")_ suggested that "the movie is not just a story. It is an experience. An experience of watching something that puts life into you, that puts a cheer on your face, however depressed you might be."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-73)_[The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times\_of\_India "The Times of India")_ wrote, "_Lagaan_ has all the attractions of big-sounding [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman") songs, excellent performances by Aamir Khan... and a successful debut for pretty Gracy Singh. In addition, there is the celebrated [David vs. Goliath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_vs_Goliath "David vs Goliath") cricket match, which has the audiences screaming and clapping."[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-74)

[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert"), writing for the _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_, gave the film 3.5 out of 4 stars and wrote, "_Lagaan_ is an enormously entertaining movie, like nothing we've ever seen before, and yet completely familiar... At the same time, it's a memory of the films we all grew up on, with clearly-defined villains and heroes, a love-triangle, and even a comic character who saves the day. _Lagaan_ is a well-crafted, hugely entertaining epic that has the spice of a foreign culture."[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-75) Derek Elley of _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ suggested that it "could be the trigger for Bollywood's long-awaited crossover to non-ethnic markets".[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-76) Somni Sengupta of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, described it as "a carnivalesque genre packed with romance, swordplay and improbable song-and-dance routines".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-77) Dave Kehr, another _New York Times_ film critic, called _Lagaan_ "a movie that knows its business -- pleasing a broad, popular audience -- and goes about it with savvy professionalism and genuine flair."[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-78) Kevin Thomas of the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ argued that the film is "an affectionate homage to a popular genre that raises it to the level of an art film with fully drawn characters, a serious underlying theme, and a sophisticated style and point of view."[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-LATimes-79)

[Peter Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bradshaw "Peter Bradshaw") of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ described the film as "a lavish epic, a gorgeous love story, and a rollicking adventure yarn. Larger than life and outrageously enjoyable, it's got a dash of [Spaghetti Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaghetti_Western "Spaghetti Western"), a hint of [Kurosawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akira_Kurosawa "Akira Kurosawa"), with a bracing shot of [Kipling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kipling "Kipling")."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-80) Kuljinder Singh of the _[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")_ stated that "_Lagaan_ is anything but standard Bollywood fodder, and is the first must-see of the Indian summer. A movie that will have you laughing and crying, but leaving with a smile."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-81)

_Lagaan_ was listed as #14 on _[Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel\_4 "Channel 4")_'s "50 Films To See Before You Die" and was the only Indian film to be listed.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-82) The film was also well received in China, where its themes resonated with Chinese audiences.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-83) It was ranked #55 in _[Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire\_(magazine) "Empire (magazine)")_ magazine's "The 100 Best Films of World Cinema" in 2010.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-84) In 2011, John Nugent of the _Trenton Independent_ called the film "a masterpiece ... and what better way to learn a bit about India's colonial experience! History and great entertainment, all rolled into one (albeit long) classic film."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-85) In 2021, American filmmaker [James Gunn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Gunn "James Gunn") named _Lagaan_ as his favorite Indian movie.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-86)

_Lagaan_".[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-usatoday-87) With [Sony Pictures Classics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Pictures_Classics "Sony Pictures Classics") distributing the film and Oscar-winning director [Baz Luhrmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baz_Luhrmann "Baz Luhrmann") praising it, _Lagaan_ had a chance to win.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-usatoday-87)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-91) The _[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")_ commented that the nomination raised [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") hopes that Indian films would become more popular in the US.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-92) In India, the nomination was celebrated with news reports about a win bringing in "a great boost for the Indian film industry"[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-93) and "a [Bharat Ratna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharat_Ratna "Bharat Ratna") for Aamir Khan and the status of a '[national film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Feature_Film "National Film Award for Best Feature Film")' for Lagaan".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-94)

When _Lagaan_ lost the award to the Bosnian film _[No Man's Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No\_Man's\_Land\_(2001\_film) "No Man's Land (2001 film)")_,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-95) there was disappointment in India. Khan said, "Certainly we were disappointed. But the thing that really kept us in our spirits was that the entire country was behind us."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-khan_oscars-96) Filmmaker [Mahesh Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahesh_Bhatt "Mahesh Bhatt") criticised the "American film industry" as "insular and the foreign category awards were given just for the sake of it."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-khan_oscars-96) Gowariker added that "Americans must learn to like our films".[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-97)

The film won a number of awards at Indian award ceremonies including eight [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards"),[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-98) eight [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"), eight [Screen Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Awards "Screen Awards")[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-99) and 10 [IIFA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Indian_Film_Academy_Awards "International Indian Film Academy Awards").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-100) Apart from these major awards, it also won awards at other national and international ceremonies.

_**Lagaan: Once Upon a Time in India**_, or simply _**Lagaan**_, (transl.Land Tax) is a 2001 Indian [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi")-language [epic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_film "Epic film")[period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_film "Period film")[sports drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_drama "Sports drama") film[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-5) written and directed by [Ashutosh Gowariker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashutosh_Gowariker "Ashutosh Gowariker"). The film was produced by [Aamir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan"), who stars alongside debutant [Gracy Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gracy_Singh "Gracy Singh") and [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_people "British people") actors [Rachel Shelley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Shelley "Rachel Shelley") and [Paul Blackthorne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Blackthorne "Paul Blackthorne"). Set in 1893, during the late [Victorian period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_era "Victorian era") of [British colonial rule in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj"), the film follows the inhabitants of a village in [Central India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India_Agency "Central India Agency"), who, burdened by high taxes and several years of drought, are challenged by an arrogant [British Indian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Indian_Army "British Indian Army") officer to a game of [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") as a wager to avoid paying the taxes they owe. The villagers face the arduous task of learning a game that is alien to them and playing for victory.

Produced on a budget of ₹25 crore (US$5.3 million), _Lagaan_ was the [most expensive Indian film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_Indian_films "List of most expensive Indian films") at the time of its release.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-6) It faced multiple challenges during production: Khan was initially sceptical about starring in a sports film, and later, prospective producers called for budget cuts and script modifications. Eventually, the film would become the maiden project of Aamir Khan Productions, and mark Khan's foray into film production. Gowariker was inspired by aspects of the sports drama _[Naya Daur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naya\_Daur\_(1957\_film) "Naya Daur (1957 film)")_ (1957) in developing the film. The language featured in the film was based on [Awadhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awadhi_language "Awadhi language"), but was diluted with standard Hindi for modern audiences. Principal photography took place in villages near [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj"). [Nitin Chandrakant Desai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitin_Chandrakant_Desai "Nitin Chandrakant Desai") served as art director, while [Bhanu Athaiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhanu_Athaiya "Bhanu Athaiya") was the costume designer. The original soundtrack was composed by [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman"), with lyrics written by [Javed Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar "Javed Akhtar").

_Lagaan_ was theatrically released in India on 15 June 2001, clashing with _[Gadar: Ek Prem Katha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gadar:\_Ek\_Prem\_Katha "Gadar: Ek Prem Katha")_. It received widespread critical acclaim for Gowariker's direction, Khan's performance, dialogues, soundtrack, and the film's [anti-imperialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-imperialist "Anti-imperialist") stance. With earnings of ₹65.97 crore (US$13.98 million) during its initial release, the film was the third [highest-grossing Hindi film of 2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Hindi_films_of_2001 "List of Hindi films of 2001"). _Lagaan_ was screened at numerous international film festivals and garnered multiple accolades. It was the third, and as of 2025 the last, Indian film to be nominated for the [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film") after _[Mother India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother\_India "Mother India")_ (1957) and _[Salaam Bombay!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salaam\_Bombay! "Salaam Bombay!")_ (1988). _Lagaan_ became the most-awarded film at the [47th Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/47th_Filmfare_Awards "47th Filmfare Awards") with eight wins, including [Best Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Film "Filmfare Award for Best Film"), [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Director "Filmfare Award for Best Director") for Gowariker and [Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor") for Khan.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-7) At the [49th National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/49th_National_Film_Awards "49th National Film Awards"), the film won eight awards, including [Best Popular Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Popular_Film_Providing_Wholesome_Entertainment "National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-8).

The film is considered to be one of the greatest films ever made in [Indian cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cinema "Indian cinema") of the 2000s.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-10)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In 1893, the farmers of the village of [Champaner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaner "Champaner"), located within the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj")[Central India Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India_Agency "Central India Agency"), endure an oppressive colonial administration. Despite a devastating drought and a failed harvest, British officials demand the regular [_lagaan_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_value_tax "Land value tax") (land tax). Led by a resilient young farmer named Bhuvan, the villagers appeal to their local ruler, Raja Puran Singh, for a tax waiver. Their petition is intercepted by the arrogant and sadistic regiment commander, Captain Andrew Russell. Russell proposes a high-stakes wager: the villagers will play a game of [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") against his elite British officers. If the villagers win, their lagaan will be completely canceled for three consecutive years; if they lose, they must pay triple the standard tax, an ultimatum that would guarantee their starvation. Bhuvan boldly accepts the challenge, and the match is scheduled three months later.

Bhuvan initially faces intense skepticism and isolation, as the terrified villagers refuse to believe they can master an unfamiliar British sport. Slowly, he recruits a diverse group of eleven players, including a [low-caste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caste_system_in_India "Caste system in India")[untouchable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Untouchability "Untouchability") named Kachra, whose [spin-bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_bowling "Spin bowling") abilities prove lethal. Meanwhile, Russell’s sister, Elizabeth, arrives from [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"). Horrified by her brother's cruelty and secretly infatuated with Bhuvan, she decides to covertly coach the village team on the rules and strategies of the game. However, a jealous villager named Lakha, who covets Gauri—the village medic's daughter currently courted by Bhuvan—agrees to act as an insider informant and saboteur for Captain Russell. As the match approaches, Russell is severely reprimanded by his superiors for wagering the government treasury, and is warned that he will be court-martialed and forced to pay the taxes himself if the British lose.

The three-day match commences outside the British cantonment. On the first day, the British team bats first and builds a formidable score, heavily aided by the villagers' technical inexperience and Lakha’s deliberate sabotage on the field. That night, Elizabeth witnesses Lakha conferring with Russell and exposes the betrayal to the villagers. When the angry locals attack Lakha, Bhuvan intervenes, offering him a chance at redemption. Conscience-stricken, Lakha plays exceptionally well on the second day, executing critical catches that trigger a sudden British collapse, capping their innings at a daunting 322 runs. Champaner's batting response starts disastrously, losing their top batsmen rapidly to aggressive British bowling.

On the third and final day, Bhuvan anchors the collapsing innings, staging a heroic resistance alongside injured teammates. The tension peaks in the final over of the game, with the villagers requiring five runs off the final delivery to achieve victory. Russell delivers the ball, and Bhuvan strikes it high into the sky. Russell catches the ball and celebrates prematurely, but the umpire signals a no-ball as Russell had crossed the boundary line while catching it, granting Champaner a six. The villagers win the match against all odds, just as dark storm clouds burst to end the long drought. Amidst the euphoric celebrations, Elizabeth watches Bhuvan and Gauri embrace, realizing her love will remain unrequited.

In the aftermath, Elizabeth bids a poignant farewell to the grateful villagers and returns to England, where she spends the rest of her life unmarried, carrying her memories of Bhuvan. The narrator reveals that the humiliated British administration immediately transfers Russell to [Central Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Africa "Central Africa") and disbands the entire provincial regiment to cover up the embarrassment. Bhuvan and Gauri are married in a grand celebration blessed by Raja Puran Singh. Although Champaner's historic triumph effectively saved the entire province from ruin, the miraculous event ultimately slipped entirely through the cracks of documented history.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Development")]

_Lagaan_ was inspired by _[Naya Daur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naya\_Daur\_(1957\_film) "Naya Daur (1957 film)")_ (1957), a [sports drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_drama "Sports drama") film directed by [B. R. Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._R._Chopra "B. R. Chopra"), written by [Akhtar Mirza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akhtar_Mirza "Akhtar Mirza") and Kamil Rashid, and starring [Dilip Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar"), [Vyjayanthimala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyjayanthimala "Vyjayanthimala") and [Ajit Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajit_Khan "Ajit Khan").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-12)

Director Gowariker has stated that it was almost impossible to make _Lagaan_. He went to Khan, who agreed to participate after hearing the detailed script. Khan had initially rejected the idea of a "sporty" film, but was "himself in tears" upon hearing the full dialogued script.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-location-13) Even after securing Khan, Gowariker had trouble finding a producer. Producers who showed interest in the script wanted budget cuts as well as script modifications. Eventually, Khan agreed to Gowariker's suggestion that he would produce the film.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-14) Khan corroborated this by saying that the faith he had in Gowariker, the story and script of the film,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw1-15) and the opportunity of starting his own production company inspired him to produce _Lagaan_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw3-16) He also said that by being a producer himself, he was able to give greater creative freedom to Gowariker. He cited an example:

> "If the director tells the producer that he wants 50 camels, the latter will probably say, 'Why not 25? Can't you manage with 25 camels?' Whereas, if he is telling me the same thing... I will not waste time asking him questions because I am also creatively aware why he needs them."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw2-17)

[Jhamu Sughand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhamu_Sughand "Jhamu Sughand") co-produced the film because he liked the emotional and patriotic story.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-toi2008-19)_Lagaan_ was made on a [then-unprecedented budget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_Indian_films "List of most expensive Indian films") of [₹](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_rupee "Indian rupee")250 million (US$5.32 million), the highest for an Indian film of the time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-budget-4)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-20)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casting")]

Gowariker first thought of [Shah Rukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan"), [Bobby Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Deol "Bobby Deol"), [Hrithik Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrithik_Roshan "Hrithik Roshan") and [Abhishek Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhishek_Bachchan "Abhishek Bachchan") for the role of Bhuvan. After Bachchan chose to enter cinema with [J. P. Dutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._P._Dutta "J. P. Dutta")'s _[Refugee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee\_(2000\_film) "Refugee (2000 film)")_ (2000), Khan was approached with the idea.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-21)

Several actresses had express interest to act in the female lead role in the film, but Khan needed someone who matched the description of the character given in the script. After considering [Rani Mukerji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rani_Mukerji "Rani Mukerji") who did not have dates to accommodate the film, [Sonali Bendre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonali_Bendre "Sonali Bendre"), [Nandita Das](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandita_Das "Nandita Das"), [Shamita Shetty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shamita_Shetty "Shamita Shetty") and [Ameesha Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ameesha_Patel "Ameesha Patel") were approached for the role,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-gracy-22) Gowariker selected Singh for the female lead because he was convinced that she was a good actress and dancer and resembled actress [Vyjayanthimala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyjayanthimala "Vyjayanthimala"). Singh, a newcomer, devoted all her time to the film.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw2-17) Since the script also demanded a British cast, Gowariker and Khan hired Danielle Roffe as one of the [casting directors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casting_(performing_arts) "Casting (performing arts)").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-23) After Danielle and Gowariker screen-tested many, Shelley and Blackthorne were chosen for the prime roles. Overall, the film cast 15 foreign actors.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-24)

[Raghubir Yadav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raghubir_Yadav "Raghubir Yadav") played the role of the legendary [Haji Nasruddin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasreddin "Nasreddin") in the teleplay _Mullah Nasiruddin_ and has given many memorable performances such as _[Mungerilal Ke Haseen Sapne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mungerilal\_Ke\_Haseen\_Sapne "Mungerilal Ke Haseen Sapne")_. Yadav was selected for the role of Bhura, a poultry farmer, based on his performance in _[Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth\_(1998\_film) "Earth (1998 film)")_ (1998). He had undergone an [appendectomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendectomy "Appendectomy") during the filming schedule and returned to complete some of his scenes.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-25)[Rajesh Vivek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Vivek "Rajesh Vivek"), who played the fortune teller Guran, was spotted by Gowariker in the film _[Junoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junoon\_(1978\_film) "Junoon (1978 film)")_ (1978). His liking for cricket helped him in his role.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-guran_intw-26)[Raj Zutshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajendranath_Zutshi "Rajendranath Zutshi")'s friendship with Khan and association in several films brought him the role of Ismail the potter after auditions.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-ismail_intw-27)[Pradeep Rawat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pradeep_Rawat_(actor) "Pradeep Rawat (actor)")'s association with Khan in _[Sarfarosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarfarosh\_(1999\_film) "Sarfarosh (1999 film)")_ (1999) brought him the role of Deva, a [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh") ex-[sepoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sepoy "Sepoy"), which was initially intended for [Mukesh Rishi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukesh_Rishi "Mukesh Rishi"). Rawat claimed that it was the highest ever compensation he received in his career.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-deva_intw-28)[Daya Shankar Pandey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daya_Shankar_Pandey "Daya Shankar Pandey"), who preferred the role of Kachra, was known to Khan and Gowariker through previous films (_[Pehla Nasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pehla\_Nasha "Pehla Nasha")_ (1993), _[Baazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baazi\_(1995\_film) "Baazi (1995 film)")_ (1995) and _[Ghulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghulam\_(film) "Ghulam (film)")_ (1998)). Pandey credited Gowariker for his acting in the film as Goli, saying that Gowariker and he would discuss the required emotions and expressions before shooting.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-29)

[Yashpal Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yashpal_Sharma_(actor) "Yashpal Sharma (actor)") was chosen by Gowariker for the role of Lakha, the woodcutter, after his portrayal in _[Samar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samar\_(1999\_film) "Samar (1999 film)")_ (1999). He said it was a good experience working with Khan and Gowariker during the film.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-30) Amin Hajee earlier worked in a film with Gowariker. The friendly association brought Gowariker to him with the script, which he liked, and thereafter he successfully auditioned for his role of Bagha, a mute drummer. His knowledge of mute people and some assistance from a music band helped him better prepare for his role. Gowariker, who believed that Amin was like [Sylvester Stallone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvester_Stallone "Sylvester Stallone"), would refer to him as Stallone during filming.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-bagha_intw-31)[Aditya Lakhia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aditya_Lakhia "Aditya Lakhia")'s association with Gowariker in _[Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabhi\_Haan\_Kabhi\_Naa "Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa")_ (1993) and _Pehla Nasha_ (1993) brought him the role of Kachra, the untouchable. He read the book _[Everybody Loves a Good Drought](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody\_Loves\_a\_Good\_Drought "Everybody Loves a Good Drought")_ by [P. Sainath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palagummi_Sainath "Palagummi Sainath") to better understand and portray his character.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-kachra_intw-32)

### Pre-production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Pre-production")]

One of the first members to join the production team was [Nitin Chandrakant Desai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitin_Chandrakant_Desai "Nitin Chandrakant Desai"), the art director, with whom Gowariker set out for extensive location hunt throughout India, to find the setting for the fictional town of Champaner, in late 1998. After searching through Rajasthan, Nasik, UP, they zeroed in on an ancient village near [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj"), located in [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat")'s [Kutch district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutch_District "Kutch District"), by May 1999, where the film was primarily shot.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-location-13)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-33)

The script demanded a dry location: an agricultural village where it had not rained in several years. To depict the 1890s era, the crew also required a village which lacked electricity, communication and automobiles.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw1-15) Kutch faced the same problems at that time and hence the village of Kunariya, located a few miles away from Bhuj, was chosen. During the filming of _Lagaan_, it did not rain at all in the region. However, a week after the shoot finished, it rained heavily bringing relief to Bhuj, which had a lean monsoon the previous year.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-gracy-22) The typical old Kutch hamlet was built by the local people four months before the arrival of the crew.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-location-13) The [2001 Gujarat earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake "2001 Gujarat earthquake") devastated this region and displaced many locals. The crew, including the English, contributed to their cause by donating ₹250,000 (equivalent to ₹1,000,000 or US$10,000 in 2023), with further contributions during the year.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-34)

[Avadhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awadhi_language "Awadhi language"), which is a [dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialect "Dialect") of [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi"), is primarily from a region in [Uttar Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uttar_Pradesh "Uttar Pradesh"). It was chosen to give the feel of the language spoken during that era. However, the language was diluted, and modern viewers can understand it.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw2-17) The dialogues, which were a combination of three dialects (Avadhi, [Bhojpuri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhojpuri_language "Bhojpuri language") and [Braj Bhasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braj_Bhasha "Braj Bhasha")) were penned by Hindi writer [K. P. Saxena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._P._Saxena "K. P. Saxena").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-gracy-22)

[Bhanu Athaiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhanu_Athaiya "Bhanu Athaiya"), who won an [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") for her work in _[Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhi\_(film) "Gandhi (film)")_ (1982), was the [costume designer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costume_designer "Costume designer") for the film. With a large number of extras, it was difficult for her to make enough costumes. She spent a lot of time researching to lend authenticity to the characters.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-gracy-22)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Filming")]

The film took approximately a year to plan, which included ten months for production and one month for the development of Khan's character, which the first-time producer found tiring. Khan obtained a crew of about 300 people for six months. Due to the lack of comfortable hotels in Bhuj, he hired a newly constructed apartment and furnished it completely for the crew. Security was set up and a special housekeeping team was brought to take care of the crew's needs.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw3-16) Most of the 19th century tools and equipment depicted in the film were lent to the crew by the local villagers. Initially, they did not want to part with their equipment, but after much coaxing, they gave in. They then travelled to different parts of the country to collect the musical instruments used in that day and era.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-aamir_intw3-16)

During the shooting, Gowariker suffered from a [slipped disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_disc_herniation "Spinal disc herniation") and had to rest for 30 days. During this period, he had his bed next to the monitor and continued with his work.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-35)

The filming schedule spanned the winter and summer, commencing in early January 2000 and finishing in mid-June. This was physically challenging for many, with the temperatures ranging from 0 to 50°C (32 to 122°F).[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-ismail_intw-27)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-bagha_intw-31) The actors had to drink frequently and sit in the shade.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-guran_intw-26)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-deva_intw-28) The schedule was strict. The day began at 6 am, changing into costumes and getting onto the actors' bus, which took them to the sets in Kanuria. The actors, including Khan, all travelled on the same bus. If anyone missed it, it was up to them to reach the sets. One day, Khan was late and missed the actors' bus. That day, his wife Reena, the executive producer, reprimanded him for being late. She told him he had to set an example for the rest of the crew. "If he started coming late, how could she tell the others to come on time?"[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-deva_intw-28) While on the sets, the actors were given call sheets with the day's timetable such as breakfast, hairstyling, make-up, costumes, etc.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-36)
