## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Release")]

Before its worldwide release, Khan kept a promise to screen the film to the locals of [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-37)_Lagaan_ clashed with [Anil Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Sharma_(director) "Anil Sharma (director)")'s _[Gadar: Ek Prem Katha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gadar:\_Ek\_Prem\_Katha "Gadar: Ek Prem Katha")_, starring [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol") and [Ameesha Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ameesha_Patel "Ameesha Patel"), at the box-office.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-39) The film made it to the UK Top 10 after its commercial release.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-40) It was the first Indian film to have a nationwide release in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China")[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-41) and had its dubbed version released in Italy.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Rediff_LIFF-42) With favorable reviews from the French press, _Lagaan_ premiered in Paris on 26 June 2002 and continued to have an unprecedented nine weeks of screening with over 45,000 people watching.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-43) It was released in the United States, Canada, France, Germany, Japan, Malaysia, Hong Kong, South Africa and the Middle East with respective [vernacular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernacular "Vernacular") subtitles.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Rediff_LIFF-42)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-44) The film took a cumulative of $2.5 million at the international box-office and ₹380 million (equivalent to ₹1.5 billion or US$16 million in 2023) at the domestic box-office.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-top-47)

In 2001, _Lagaan_ had a world premiere at the [International Indian Film Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Indian_Film_Academy_Awards "International Indian Film Academy Awards") (IIFA) weekend in [Sun City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_City,_North_West "Sun City, North West"), South Africa.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-48) The [Locarno International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locarno_International_Film_Festival "Locarno International Film Festival") authorities published the rules of cricket before the film was screened to a crowd which reportedly danced to its soundtrack in the aisles.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-49)_Lagaan_ was shown 4 times due to public demand as against the usual norm of showcasing films once at the festival.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Rediff_LIFF-42) It subsequently won the Prix du Public Award at the festival.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-50) After the film's publicity in Locarno, the director, Gowariker said that distributors from Switzerland, Italy, France, Netherlands, North Africa, Finland and Germany were wanting to purchase the distribution rights.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Rediff_LIFF-42) Special screenings were held in Russia, where people were keen to watch the film after its Oscar nomination.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-51)

Apart from these screenings, it was shown at the [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival"),[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-52)[Cairo International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairo_International_Film_Festival "Cairo International Film Festival"),[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-53)[Stockholm International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_International_Film_Festival "Stockholm International Film Festival"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-54)[Helsinki Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki_Film_Festival "Helsinki Film Festival")[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-55) and the [Toronto International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_International_Film_Festival "Toronto International Film Festival").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-56) The film is available on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-57)

### Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Home media")]

There were two releases for the DVD. The first, as a 2-DVD set, was released on 27 May 2002 in limited regions. It contained subtitles in [Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"), English, Hebrew, Hindi, Turkish and several European languages. It is available in 16:9 Anamorphic widescreen, Dolby Digital 5.1 Surround, progressive 24 frame/s, widescreen and NTSC format. It carried an additional fifteen minutes of deleted scenes, filmographies and trailers.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-58)

The second was released as anniversary edition 3-disc DVD box after 6 years of the theatrical release. This also included _Chale Chalo_ which was a documentary on the making of _Lagaan_, a curtain-raiser on the making of the soundtrack, deleted scenes, trailers, along with other collectibles such as 11 collector cards, a collectible _Lagaan_ coin embossed with the character of _Bhuvan_, a 35 mm [CinemaScope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScope "CinemaScope") filmstrip hand-cut from the film's filmstrip were bundled with the film.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-lagaandvd-59) After its release, it became the highest-selling DVD in India, beating _[Sholay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sholay "Sholay")_ (1975).[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-60)_Chale Chalo – The Lunacy of Film Making_, won the [National Film Award for Best Exploration/Adventure Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Exploration/Adventure_Film "National Film Award for Best Exploration/Adventure Film").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-lagaandvd-59)

A comic book, _Lagaan: The Story_, along with 2 colouring books, a mask book and a cricket [board game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_game "Board game") were subsequently released to the commercial market. The comic book, available in English and Hindi, was targeted at children between the ages of 6 and 14. At the book's launch, Aamir Khan said that they were keen to turn the film into a comic strip during the pre-production phase itself.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-62)

In March 2002, a book titled _The Spirit of Lagaan – The Extraordinary Story of the Creators of a Classic_ was published. It covers the making of the film, describing in detail the setbacks and obstacles that the crew faced while developing the film from concept to its release.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-63)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Box office")]

The film initially grossed [₹](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_rupee "Indian rupee")65.97 crore (equivalent to ₹263 crore or US$27 million in 2023) worldwide in 2001. This made it the third [highest-grossing Hindi film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_Hindi_films "List of highest-grossing Hindi films") of 2001, behind _[Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabhi\_Khushi\_Kabhie\_Gham "Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham")_ and _[Gadar: Ek Prem Katha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gadar:\_Ek\_Prem\_Katha "Gadar: Ek Prem Katha")_.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-64)

Domestically, _Lagaan_ grossed ₹55.13 crore (equivalent to ₹219 crore or US$23 million in 2023) in India. Its domestic [net income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net_income "Net income") was ₹34.31 crore, equivalent to ₹187 crore ($25 million) when adjusted for inflation.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-boi-65)

With an overseas gross of ₹10.84 crore[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-top-47) ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")2.2 million) in 2001, it was the year's second [highest-grossing Indian film overseas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_Indian_films "List of highest-grossing Indian films"), preceded only by _Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham_.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-66)_Lagaan_'s overseas gross included [£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_sterling "Pound sterling")600,000 in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), US$910,000 in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"), and US$180,000 in the [Arab states of the Persian Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_states_of_the_Persian_Gulf "Arab states of the Persian Gulf").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-boi-65)

In [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), where the film released on 16 May 2003, it grossed [¥](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renminbi "Renminbi")3 million,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-67) equivalent to ₹ 1.71 crore[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-68) (US$362,500).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-69)

Including the film's China collections, the film's total worldwide gross was ₹67.68 crore (US$14.533 million).[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-70)

### Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

_Lagaan_ was met with critical acclaim. On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 95% of 64 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 7.9/10.The website's consensus reads: "Lagaan is lavish, rousing entertainment in the old-fashioned tradition of Hollywood musicals."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-71)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned the film a score of 84 out of 100, based on 21 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-Metacritic-72)

Sudish Kamath of _[The Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hindu "The Hindu")_ suggested that "the movie is not just a story. It is an experience. An experience of watching something that puts life into you, that puts a cheer on your face, however depressed you might be."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-73)_[The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times\_of\_India "The Times of India")_ wrote, "_Lagaan_ has all the attractions of big-sounding [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman") songs, excellent performances by Aamir Khan... and a successful debut for pretty Gracy Singh. In addition, there is the celebrated [David vs. Goliath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_vs_Goliath "David vs Goliath") cricket match, which has the audiences screaming and clapping."[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-74)

[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert"), writing for the _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_, gave the film 3.5 out of 4 stars and wrote, "_Lagaan_ is an enormously entertaining movie, like nothing we've ever seen before, and yet completely familiar... At the same time, it's a memory of the films we all grew up on, with clearly-defined villains and heroes, a love-triangle, and even a comic character who saves the day. _Lagaan_ is a well-crafted, hugely entertaining epic that has the spice of a foreign culture."[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-75) Derek Elley of _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ suggested that it "could be the trigger for Bollywood's long-awaited crossover to non-ethnic markets".[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-76) Somni Sengupta of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, described it as "a carnivalesque genre packed with romance, swordplay and improbable song-and-dance routines".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-77) Dave Kehr, another _New York Times_ film critic, called _Lagaan_ "a movie that knows its business -- pleasing a broad, popular audience -- and goes about it with savvy professionalism and genuine flair."[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-78) Kevin Thomas of the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ argued that the film is "an affectionate homage to a popular genre that raises it to the level of an art film with fully drawn characters, a serious underlying theme, and a sophisticated style and point of view."[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-LATimes-79)

[Peter Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bradshaw "Peter Bradshaw") of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ described the film as "a lavish epic, a gorgeous love story, and a rollicking adventure yarn. Larger than life and outrageously enjoyable, it's got a dash of [Spaghetti Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaghetti_Western "Spaghetti Western"), a hint of [Kurosawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akira_Kurosawa "Akira Kurosawa"), with a bracing shot of [Kipling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kipling "Kipling")."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-80) Kuljinder Singh of the _[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")_ stated that "_Lagaan_ is anything but standard Bollywood fodder, and is the first must-see of the Indian summer. A movie that will have you laughing and crying, but leaving with a smile."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-81)

_Lagaan_ was listed as #14 on _[Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel\_4 "Channel 4")_'s "50 Films To See Before You Die" and was the only Indian film to be listed.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-82) The film was also well received in China, where its themes resonated with Chinese audiences.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-83) It was ranked #55 in _[Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire\_(magazine) "Empire (magazine)")_ magazine's "The 100 Best Films of World Cinema" in 2010.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-84) In 2011, John Nugent of the _Trenton Independent_ called the film "a masterpiece ... and what better way to learn a bit about India's colonial experience! History and great entertainment, all rolled into one (albeit long) classic film."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-85) In 2021, American filmmaker [James Gunn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Gunn "James Gunn") named _Lagaan_ as his favorite Indian movie.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-86)

## Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Lagaan&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Awards")]

Main article: [List of accolades received by Lagaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accolades_received_by_Lagaan "List of accolades received by Lagaan")

Aamir Khan and Gowariker went to Los Angeles to generate publicity for the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award"). Khan said, "We just started showing it to whoever we could, even the hotel staff."[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-usatoday-87) About India's official entry to the 2002 Oscars, _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ wrote, "A Bollywood film that portrays the British in India as ruthless sadists and Mafia-style crooks has been chosen as Delhi's official entry to the Academy Awards."[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-telegraphuk-88) It added that the film was expected to win the nomination.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-telegraphuk-88)

On 12 February 2002, _Lagaan_ was nominated for the [best foreign language film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_submissions_to_the_74th_Academy_Awards_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "List of submissions to the 74th Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film") at the Academy Award nominations ceremony.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-89) After the nomination, Khan reacted by saying, "To see the name of the film and actually hear it being nominated was very satisfying".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-90) Post-nomination reactions poured in from several parts of the world. _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA\_Today "USA Today")_ wrote "Hooray for [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood"), and India's _Lagaan_".[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-usatoday-87) With [Sony Pictures Classics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Pictures_Classics "Sony Pictures Classics") distributing the film and Oscar-winning director [Baz Luhrmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baz_Luhrmann "Baz Luhrmann") praising it, _Lagaan_ had a chance to win.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-usatoday-87)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-91) The _[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")_ commented that the nomination raised [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") hopes that Indian films would become more popular in the US.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-92) In India, the nomination was celebrated with news reports about a win bringing in "a great boost for the Indian film industry"[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-93) and "a [Bharat Ratna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharat_Ratna "Bharat Ratna") for Aamir Khan and the status of a '[national film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Feature_Film "National Film Award for Best Feature Film")' for Lagaan".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-94)

When _Lagaan_ lost the award to the Bosnian film _[No Man's Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No\_Man's\_Land\_(2001\_film) "No Man's Land (2001 film)")_,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-95) there was disappointment in India. Khan said, "Certainly we were disappointed. But the thing that really kept us in our spirits was that the entire country was behind us."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-khan_oscars-96) Filmmaker [Mahesh Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahesh_Bhatt "Mahesh Bhatt") criticised the "American film industry" as "insular and the foreign category awards were given just for the sake of it."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-khan_oscars-96) Gowariker added that "Americans must learn to like our films".[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-97)

The film won a number of awards at Indian award ceremonies including eight [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards"),[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-98) eight [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"), eight [Screen Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Awards "Screen Awards")[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-99) and 10 [IIFA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Indian_Film_Academy_Awards "International Indian Film Academy Awards").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagaan#cite_note-100) Apart from these major awards, it also won awards at other national and international ceremonies.

The [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China") competed at the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), Australia. The team excluded athletes from the [Special Administrative Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Administrative_Region_of_the_People's_Republic_of_China "Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China") of Hong Kong, after the territory's [return](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_of_sovereignty_over_Hong_Kong "Transfer of sovereignty over Hong Kong") to Chinese rule in 1997, and which competed separately as _[Hong Kong, China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong\_Kong,\_China\_at\_the\_2000\_Summer\_Olympics "Hong Kong, China at the 2000 Summer Olympics")_.

Sydney 2000 marked the first time the Chinese Olympic team competed in Australia as China boycotted the [1956 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Summer_Olympics "1956 Summer Olympics") in [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne") due to the participation of [Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China_at_the_1956_Summer_Olympics "Republic of China at the 1956 Summer Olympics") at these games.

271 competitors, 91 men and 180 women, took part in 163 events in 28 sports.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-sports-reference-1) China finished for the first time in the top 3 with 28 gold medals.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Results-2) China also broke the record for the most gold medals won by Asian countries at a single Summer Olympics (28), which was previously set by Japan in [1964](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics "1964 Summer Olympics") (16) and by China in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics "1992 Summer Olympics") (16) and [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") (16).

The [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China") competed at the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), Australia. The team excluded athletes from the [Special Administrative Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Administrative_Region_of_the_People's_Republic_of_China "Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China") of Hong Kong, after the territory's [return](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_of_sovereignty_over_Hong_Kong "Transfer of sovereignty over Hong Kong") to Chinese rule in 1997, and which competed separately as _[Hong Kong, China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong\_Kong,\_China\_at\_the\_2000\_Summer\_Olympics "Hong Kong, China at the 2000 Summer Olympics")_.

Sydney 2000 marked the first time the Chinese Olympic team competed in Australia as China boycotted the [1956 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Summer_Olympics "1956 Summer Olympics") in [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne") due to the participation of [Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China_at_the_1956_Summer_Olympics "Republic of China at the 1956 Summer Olympics") at these games.

271 competitors, 91 men and 180 women, took part in 163 events in 28 sports.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-sports-reference-1) China finished for the first time in the top 3 with 28 gold medals.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Results-2) China also broke the record for the most gold medals won by Asian countries at a single Summer Olympics (28), which was previously set by Japan in [1964](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics "1964 Summer Olympics") (16) and by China in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics "1992 Summer Olympics") (16) and [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") (16).

An [earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake "Earthquake") struck India and Pakistan on 26 January 2001 at 08:46 am IST. The [epicentre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epicentre "Epicentre") was about 9 km south-southwest of the village of [Chobari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chobari "Chobari") in [Bhachau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhachau "Bhachau")[Taluka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taluka "Taluka") of [Kutch district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutch_district "Kutch district") in [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat"), India.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-3) The earthquake had a maximum [Mercalli intensity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercalli_intensity "Mercalli intensity") of XII (_Extreme_).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4)

The [intraplate earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intraplate_earthquake "Intraplate earthquake") measured 7.6 on the [moment magnitude scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moment_magnitude_scale "Moment magnitude scale") and occurred at a depth of 17.4 km (10.8 mi).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-ISC-GEM-1) The earthquake killed at least 20,023 people, injured another 166,000 and destroyed about 400,000 buildings in Gujarat and the Pakistani province of [Sindh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sindh "Sindh").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-APR2001UPDATE-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-USGS-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-7) The vast majority of deaths and damage were observed in [Kutch district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutch_district "Kutch district"), while nearly 1,600 additional deaths occurred in the cities of [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad"), [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkot "Rajkot"), [Jamnagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamnagar "Jamnagar"), [Surendranagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surendranagar "Surendranagar"), [Surat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surat "Surat"), [Gandhinagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhinagar "Gandhinagar") and [Vadodara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadodara "Vadodara").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-UNDMT-8)

## Tectonic setting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Tectonic setting")]

See also: [Geology of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology_of_India "Geology of India")

[Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat") lies 300–400 km from the plate boundary between the [Indian plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_plate "Indian plate") and the [Eurasian plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurasian_plate "Eurasian plate"), but the current tectonics are still governed by the effects of the continuing [continental collision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_collision "Continental collision") along this boundary. During the break-up of [Gondwana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gondwana "Gondwana") in the [Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic "Jurassic"), this area was affected by [rifting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift "Rift") with a roughly west–east trend. During the collision with Eurasia the area has undergone shortening, involving both reactivation of the original rift [faults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fault_(geology) "Fault (geology)") and development of new low-angle [thrust faults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrust_fault "Thrust fault"). The related [folding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fold_(geology) "Fold (geology)") has formed a series of ranges, particularly in central Kutch.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-9)

The [focal mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focal_mechanism "Focal mechanism") of most earthquakes is consistent with reverse faulting on [reactivated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inversion_(geology) "Inversion (geology)") rift faults. The pattern of uplift and subsidence associated with the [1819 Rann of Kutch earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1819_Rann_of_Kutch_earthquake "1819 Rann of Kutch earthquake") is consistent with reactivation of such a fault.

The earthquake was caused by movement on a previously unknown south-dipping fault, trending parallel to the inferred rift structures.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-Bodin-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-Li_Liu_Yang_pp._255%E2%80%93264-12) No major surface ruptures were associated with the shock, classifying it as a blind thrust earthquake. Lateral spreading was widely reported and strike-slip faulting was observed at Bharodia and Manfara.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-13) On the [moment magnitude scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moment_magnitude_scale "Moment magnitude scale"), the [International Seismological Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Seismological_Centre "International Seismological Centre") said it measured a magnitude of 7.6,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-ISC-GEM-1) while the [United States Geological Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Geological_Survey "United States Geological Survey") put it at 7.7.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-ANSS-14)

### Rupture propagation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Rupture propagation")]

A finite fault model from the USGS estimated that the [earthquake rupture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake_rupture "Earthquake rupture") had an area of 141 km (88 mi) x 18 km (11 mi), lasting approximately 25 seconds. Slip was mostly concentrated around the northern patches of the rupture, with a maximum slip of 9.695 m (31.81 ft) recorded in the village of [Chobari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chobari "Chobari"). The full rupture also extended through the cities of [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj") and [Rapar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapar "Rapar"), although slip in these areas was extremely minor.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-ANSS-14) Despite the large magnitude and rupture area, no visible [surface ruptures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface_ruptures "Surface ruptures") could be identified in the [epicentral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epicenter "Epicenter") area.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-sudhirjain-15)

### Ground motion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Ground motion")]

The earthquake had a maximum [Modified Mercalli intensity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modified_Mercalli_intensity "Modified Mercalli intensity") of IX-XII (_Violent_-_Extreme_).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4) It also registered X (_Devastating_) on the [Medvedev–Sponheuer–Karnik scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medvedev%E2%80%93Sponheuer%E2%80%93Karnik_scale "Medvedev–Sponheuer–Karnik scale"), with the maximum intensity observed over an east-northeast elongated zone of approximately 2,100 km 2 (810 mi 2); much of Gujarat recorded tremors of VII (_Very Strong_) or higher. [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad") recorded a maximum [peak ground acceleration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peak_ground_acceleration "Peak ground acceleration") of 0.11 _g_. Shaking from the earthquake lasted several minutes, with stronger ground motion lasting at least 85 seconds. Numerous rockfalls and landslides occurred in the [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj") and [Bhachau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhachau "Bhachau") areas. There was extensive evidence of [soil liquefaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil_liquefaction "Soil liquefaction") at the [Rann of Kutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rann_of_Kutch "Rann of Kutch"), [Banni Grasslands Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banni_Grasslands_Reserve "Banni Grasslands Reserve"), coastal areas of the [Gulf of Kutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Kutch "Gulf of Kutch") and numerous [sand boils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sand_boil "Sand boil") in dry lakebeds northeast of [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj"). After the earthquake, these sand boils had fountains of saline [groundwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groundwater "Groundwater") rising 2–3 m (6.6–9.8 ft). Widespread [subsidence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subsidence "Subsidence") and lateral spreading also occurred at [Kandla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Kandla "Port of Kandla") and [Navlakhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Navlakhi "Port of Navlakhi") ports.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-sudhirjain-15)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4)

### Aftershocks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Aftershocks")]

By 31 December 2001, there were 107 aftershocks exceeding M w 4.0 which were recorded by the USGS, including 9 events measuring M w 5.0 or higher; most aftershocks occurred south of the epicenter near [Bhachau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhachau "Bhachau").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-16) The largest aftershock occurred on 28 January, had a magnitude of M wc 5.8 and was located 15 km (9.3 mi) west-southwest of [Rapar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapar "Rapar").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-17)

The [United States Geological Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Geological_Survey "United States Geological Survey")'s [PAGER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PAGER "PAGER")-CAT catalog reported 20,023 fatalities.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-PAGER-CAT-20) Additionally, 166,836 injuries were recorded,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-USGS-6) a total of 28 million people across [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat") were affected, and 442 villages lost at least 70% of houses.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-NIDM-19) In [Kutch District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutch_District "Kutch District"), 90% of homes were damaged or destroyed, with 24% of the housing stock affected overall in Gujarat; most affected buildings were non-engineered, unreinforced [stonemasonry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonemasonry "Stonemasonry"), although many reinforced concrete buildings also collapsed. Water outages were widespread due to liquefaction and [soil compaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil_compaction "Soil compaction"), with many [pumping stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pumping_stations "Pumping stations") and two water towers collapsing in the affected area. However, damage to highways and bridges was relatively minor.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4) Economic losses amounted to US$10 billion.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-21)

[Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj"), one of the closest cities to the epicenter, was devastated, with roughly 10,000 people killed[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-nyt-22) and 95% of buildings destroyed or uninhabitable after the quake;[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-23) 38,653 homes partially or fully collapsed in the city.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-24) The quake also destroyed eight schools, two hospitals and 4 km of road in Bhuj, and partly destroyed the historic [Swaminarayan temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shri_Swaminarayan_Mandir,_Bhuj "Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Bhuj") and historic forts, [Prag Mahal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prag_Mahal "Prag Mahal") and [Aina Mahal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aina_Mahal "Aina Mahal"). The [Indian National Trust for Arts and Cultural Heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Trust_for_Art_and_Cultural_Heritage "Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage") (INTACH) inspected more than 250 heritage buildings in Kutch and Saurashtra and found that about 40% of them either collapsed or were seriously damaged; only 10% were undamaged.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-25) Bhuj's district hospital collapsed, killing about 193 people inside,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-NIDM-19) while at the city's main [telephone exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_exchange "Telephone exchange") building, 50% of its walls collapsed, damaging interior electrical controls and resulting in many casualties.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4)

Over 1.2 million houses in 8,000 villages and 490 towns were damaged or destroyed, as well as 12,000 schools, 2,000 health facilities, many historic buildings and tourist attractions;[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-IIFEAD-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-28) 400,000 of the damaged homes completely collapsed.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-APR2001UPDATE-5) Across [Bhachau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhachau "Bhachau"), over 5,000 people died and 9,000 houses were damaged or destroyed.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-IIFEAD-26) In [Chobari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chobari "Chobari"), the closest settlement to the epicenter, all 3,200 houses were razed and 648 residents were killed.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-29) Over 400 were also feared dead in [Rapar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapar "Rapar").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-geer-30) Adhoi village lost 354 residents, including 25 students at a school. Much of [Vondh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vondh "Vondh") was also razed and 400 people died there.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-IIFEAD-26) All 208 houses in the village of [Visnagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visnagar "Visnagar") were also destroyed.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-31) In [Anjar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anjar,_Gujarat "Anjar, Gujarat"), over 2,000 people died, including 204 who were killed at a [Republic Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Day_(India) "Republic Day (India)") parade.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-32) There were also nearly 2,000 deaths in [Gandhidham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhidham "Gandhidham"), where 30 high-rise buildings collapsed,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-33) and in nearby [Kandla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandla "Kandla"), roads and facilities at the [Port of Kandla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Kandla "Port of Kandla") were badly affected.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-geer-30) At the [Navlakhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Navlakhi "Port of Navlakhi"), extensive subsidence caused the main access road and port to drop below [sea level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level "Sea level") at high tide, preventing goods from being imported; lateral spreading caused a newly built reinforced concrete wharf to collapse into the sea.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4) Ten people were killed and all 940 homes were badly damaged in Dhori village, including 914 which were completely razed by the quake, along with multiple health centers, schools, a water tower, the mosque and three Hindu temples.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-nyt-22) In [Khavda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khavda "Khavda"), 240 people died, thousands more were injured, 20% of homes collapsed and 40% of others were moderately damaged. There were also 225 deaths in [Ratnal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratnal "Ratnal").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-34)

In [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad"), 1,021 apartments and 82 houses collapsed, and 752 people were killed.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-NIDM-19) Collapsing multistory buildings also caused deaths in [Morbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morbi "Morbi") and [Surat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surat "Surat").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-sudhirjain-15) The [Indian military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces "Indian Armed Forces") provided emergency support which was later augmented by the [International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_Red_Cross_and_Red_Crescent_Societies "International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies"). A temporary [Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cross "Red Cross") hospital remained in Bhuj to provide care while a replacement hospital was built.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-35)

There were also 19 deaths in [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-36) The [Badin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badin_District "Badin District")-[Tharparkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tharparkar "Tharparkar") area recorded 12 deaths, 115 injuries, 1,989 collapsed homes and 43,643 damaged homes.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-37) Liquefaction from the earthquake resulted in [sugarcane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarcane "Sugarcane") farms being flooded, affecting crops in the village of Kadhan.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-geer-30)

## Reconstruction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Reconstruction")]

Four months after the earthquake the [Gujarat government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Gujarat "Government of Gujarat") announced the Gujarat Earthquake Reconstruction and Rehabilitation Policy. The policy proposed a different approach to urban and rural construction with the estimated cost of rebuilding to be US$1.77 billion.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:0-38)

The main objectives of the policy included repairing, building, and strengthening houses and public buildings. Other objectives included the revival of the economy, health support, and reconstruction of the community and social infrastructure.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:0-38)

### Housing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Housing")]

The housing policies focused on the removal of rubble, setting up temporary shelters, full reconstruction of damaged houses, and the [retrofitting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retrofitting "Retrofitting") of undamaged units. The policy established a community-driven housing recovery process. The communities affected by the earthquake were given the option for complete or partial relocation to [in-situ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_situ "In situ") reconstruction.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-39) The total number of eligible houses to be repaired was 929,682 and the total number of eligible houses to be reconstructed was 213,685. By 2003, 882,896 (94%) houses were repaired and 113,271 (53%) were reconstructed.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:2-40)

### City planning

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: City planning")]

The Environmental Planning Collaborative (EPC) was commissioned to provide a new city plan for the city of [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:1-41) The plan focused on creating a wider roadway network to provide emergency access to the city. The EPC used land readjustment (LR) in the form of eight town planning schemes.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:1-41) This was implemented by deducting land from private lot sizes to create adequate public land for the widening of roadways.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-42) The remaining land was readjusted and given back to the original owners as final plots.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:1-41)

## Memorials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Memorials")]

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Smritivan_2001_Gujarat_earthquake_memorial_garden_in_Bhuj%2C_Gujarat%2C_India.jpg/250px-Smritivan_2001_Gujarat_earthquake_memorial_garden_in_Bhuj%2C_Gujarat%2C_India.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Smritivan_2001_Gujarat_earthquake_memorial_garden_in_Bhuj,_Gujarat,_India.jpg)

Smritivan

[Smritivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smritivan_Earthquake_Memorial_and_Museum "Smritivan Earthquake Memorial and Museum"), a memorial park and museum dedicated to victims of the earthquake was built on top of [Bhujia Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhujia_Hill "Bhujia Hill") in [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj"), [Kutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutch_district "Kutch district") and opened in 2022. Spread over an area of 470 acres, it has more than 13,805 trees, each dedicated to a victim, planted in the garden and 108 small water reservoirs created on the hill.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-Ray-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-46)

[Veer Balak Smarak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veer_Balak_Smarak "Veer Balak Smarak") in [Anjar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anjar,_Gujarat "Anjar, Gujarat") is a memorial dedicated to 185 school children and 20 teachers who died during the earthquake.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-ht1-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-etv-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-49)

An [earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake "Earthquake") struck India and Pakistan on 26 January 2001 at 08:46 am IST. The [epicentre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epicentre "Epicentre") was about 9 km south-southwest of the village of [Chobari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chobari "Chobari") in [Bhachau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhachau "Bhachau")[Taluka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taluka "Taluka") of [Kutch district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutch_district "Kutch district") in [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat"), India.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-3) The earthquake had a maximum [Mercalli intensity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercalli_intensity "Mercalli intensity") of XII (_Extreme_).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4)

The [intraplate earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intraplate_earthquake "Intraplate earthquake") measured 7.6 on the [moment magnitude scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moment_magnitude_scale "Moment magnitude scale") and occurred at a depth of 17.4 km (10.8 mi).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-ISC-GEM-1) The earthquake killed at least 20,023 people, injured another 166,000 and destroyed about 400,000 buildings in Gujarat and the Pakistani province of [Sindh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sindh "Sindh").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-APR2001UPDATE-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-USGS-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-7) The vast majority of deaths and damage were observed in [Kutch district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutch_district "Kutch district"), while nearly 1,600 additional deaths occurred in the cities of [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad"), [Rajkot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkot "Rajkot"), [Jamnagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamnagar "Jamnagar"), [Surendranagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surendranagar "Surendranagar"), [Surat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surat "Surat"), [Gandhinagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhinagar "Gandhinagar") and [Vadodara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadodara "Vadodara").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-UNDMT-8)

## Tectonic setting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Tectonic setting")]

See also: [Geology of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology_of_India "Geology of India")

[Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat") lies 300–400 km from the plate boundary between the [Indian plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_plate "Indian plate") and the [Eurasian plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurasian_plate "Eurasian plate"), but the current tectonics are still governed by the effects of the continuing [continental collision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_collision "Continental collision") along this boundary. During the break-up of [Gondwana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gondwana "Gondwana") in the [Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic "Jurassic"), this area was affected by [rifting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift "Rift") with a roughly west–east trend. During the collision with Eurasia the area has undergone shortening, involving both reactivation of the original rift [faults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fault_(geology) "Fault (geology)") and development of new low-angle [thrust faults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrust_fault "Thrust fault"). The related [folding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fold_(geology) "Fold (geology)") has formed a series of ranges, particularly in central Kutch.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-9)

The [focal mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focal_mechanism "Focal mechanism") of most earthquakes is consistent with reverse faulting on [reactivated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inversion_(geology) "Inversion (geology)") rift faults. The pattern of uplift and subsidence associated with the [1819 Rann of Kutch earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1819_Rann_of_Kutch_earthquake "1819 Rann of Kutch earthquake") is consistent with reactivation of such a fault.

The earthquake was caused by movement on a previously unknown south-dipping fault, trending parallel to the inferred rift structures.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-Bodin-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-Li_Liu_Yang_pp._255%E2%80%93264-12) No major surface ruptures were associated with the shock, classifying it as a blind thrust earthquake. Lateral spreading was widely reported and strike-slip faulting was observed at Bharodia and Manfara.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-13) On the [moment magnitude scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moment_magnitude_scale "Moment magnitude scale"), the [International Seismological Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Seismological_Centre "International Seismological Centre") said it measured a magnitude of 7.6,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-ISC-GEM-1) while the [United States Geological Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Geological_Survey "United States Geological Survey") put it at 7.7.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-ANSS-14)

### Rupture propagation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Rupture propagation")]

A finite fault model from the USGS estimated that the [earthquake rupture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake_rupture "Earthquake rupture") had an area of 141 km (88 mi) x 18 km (11 mi), lasting approximately 25 seconds. Slip was mostly concentrated around the northern patches of the rupture, with a maximum slip of 9.695 m (31.81 ft) recorded in the village of [Chobari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chobari "Chobari"). The full rupture also extended through the cities of [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj") and [Rapar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapar "Rapar"), although slip in these areas was extremely minor.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-ANSS-14) Despite the large magnitude and rupture area, no visible [surface ruptures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface_ruptures "Surface ruptures") could be identified in the [epicentral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epicenter "Epicenter") area.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-sudhirjain-15)

### Ground motion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Ground motion")]

The earthquake had a maximum [Modified Mercalli intensity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modified_Mercalli_intensity "Modified Mercalli intensity") of IX-XII (_Violent_-_Extreme_).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4) It also registered X (_Devastating_) on the [Medvedev–Sponheuer–Karnik scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medvedev%E2%80%93Sponheuer%E2%80%93Karnik_scale "Medvedev–Sponheuer–Karnik scale"), with the maximum intensity observed over an east-northeast elongated zone of approximately 2,100 km 2 (810 mi 2); much of Gujarat recorded tremors of VII (_Very Strong_) or higher. [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad") recorded a maximum [peak ground acceleration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peak_ground_acceleration "Peak ground acceleration") of 0.11 _g_. Shaking from the earthquake lasted several minutes, with stronger ground motion lasting at least 85 seconds. Numerous rockfalls and landslides occurred in the [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj") and [Bhachau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhachau "Bhachau") areas. There was extensive evidence of [soil liquefaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil_liquefaction "Soil liquefaction") at the [Rann of Kutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rann_of_Kutch "Rann of Kutch"), [Banni Grasslands Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banni_Grasslands_Reserve "Banni Grasslands Reserve"), coastal areas of the [Gulf of Kutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Kutch "Gulf of Kutch") and numerous [sand boils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sand_boil "Sand boil") in dry lakebeds northeast of [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj"). After the earthquake, these sand boils had fountains of saline [groundwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groundwater "Groundwater") rising 2–3 m (6.6–9.8 ft). Widespread [subsidence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subsidence "Subsidence") and lateral spreading also occurred at [Kandla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Kandla "Port of Kandla") and [Navlakhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Navlakhi "Port of Navlakhi") ports.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-sudhirjain-15)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4)

### Aftershocks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Aftershocks")]

By 31 December 2001, there were 107 aftershocks exceeding M w 4.0 which were recorded by the USGS, including 9 events measuring M w 5.0 or higher; most aftershocks occurred south of the epicenter near [Bhachau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhachau "Bhachau").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-16) The largest aftershock occurred on 28 January, had a magnitude of M wc 5.8 and was located 15 km (9.3 mi) west-southwest of [Rapar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapar "Rapar").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-17)

The [United States Geological Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Geological_Survey "United States Geological Survey")'s [PAGER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PAGER "PAGER")-CAT catalog reported 20,023 fatalities.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-PAGER-CAT-20) Additionally, 166,836 injuries were recorded,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-USGS-6) a total of 28 million people across [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat") were affected, and 442 villages lost at least 70% of houses.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-NIDM-19) In [Kutch District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutch_District "Kutch District"), 90% of homes were damaged or destroyed, with 24% of the housing stock affected overall in Gujarat; most affected buildings were non-engineered, unreinforced [stonemasonry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonemasonry "Stonemasonry"), although many reinforced concrete buildings also collapsed. Water outages were widespread due to liquefaction and [soil compaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil_compaction "Soil compaction"), with many [pumping stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pumping_stations "Pumping stations") and two water towers collapsing in the affected area. However, damage to highways and bridges was relatively minor.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4) Economic losses amounted to US$10 billion.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-21)

[Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj"), one of the closest cities to the epicenter, was devastated, with roughly 10,000 people killed[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-nyt-22) and 95% of buildings destroyed or uninhabitable after the quake;[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-23) 38,653 homes partially or fully collapsed in the city.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-24) The quake also destroyed eight schools, two hospitals and 4 km of road in Bhuj, and partly destroyed the historic [Swaminarayan temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shri_Swaminarayan_Mandir,_Bhuj "Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Bhuj") and historic forts, [Prag Mahal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prag_Mahal "Prag Mahal") and [Aina Mahal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aina_Mahal "Aina Mahal"). The [Indian National Trust for Arts and Cultural Heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Trust_for_Art_and_Cultural_Heritage "Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage") (INTACH) inspected more than 250 heritage buildings in Kutch and Saurashtra and found that about 40% of them either collapsed or were seriously damaged; only 10% were undamaged.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-25) Bhuj's district hospital collapsed, killing about 193 people inside,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-NIDM-19) while at the city's main [telephone exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_exchange "Telephone exchange") building, 50% of its walls collapsed, damaging interior electrical controls and resulting in many casualties.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4)

Over 1.2 million houses in 8,000 villages and 490 towns were damaged or destroyed, as well as 12,000 schools, 2,000 health facilities, many historic buildings and tourist attractions;[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-IIFEAD-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-28) 400,000 of the damaged homes completely collapsed.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-APR2001UPDATE-5) Across [Bhachau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhachau "Bhachau"), over 5,000 people died and 9,000 houses were damaged or destroyed.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-IIFEAD-26) In [Chobari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chobari "Chobari"), the closest settlement to the epicenter, all 3,200 houses were razed and 648 residents were killed.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-29) Over 400 were also feared dead in [Rapar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapar "Rapar").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-geer-30) Adhoi village lost 354 residents, including 25 students at a school. Much of [Vondh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vondh "Vondh") was also razed and 400 people died there.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-IIFEAD-26) All 208 houses in the village of [Visnagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visnagar "Visnagar") were also destroyed.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-31) In [Anjar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anjar,_Gujarat "Anjar, Gujarat"), over 2,000 people died, including 204 who were killed at a [Republic Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Day_(India) "Republic Day (India)") parade.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-32) There were also nearly 2,000 deaths in [Gandhidham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhidham "Gandhidham"), where 30 high-rise buildings collapsed,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-33) and in nearby [Kandla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandla "Kandla"), roads and facilities at the [Port of Kandla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Kandla "Port of Kandla") were badly affected.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-geer-30) At the [Navlakhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Navlakhi "Port of Navlakhi"), extensive subsidence caused the main access road and port to drop below [sea level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level "Sea level") at high tide, preventing goods from being imported; lateral spreading caused a newly built reinforced concrete wharf to collapse into the sea.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-asoce-4) Ten people were killed and all 940 homes were badly damaged in Dhori village, including 914 which were completely razed by the quake, along with multiple health centers, schools, a water tower, the mosque and three Hindu temples.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-nyt-22) In [Khavda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khavda "Khavda"), 240 people died, thousands more were injured, 20% of homes collapsed and 40% of others were moderately damaged. There were also 225 deaths in [Ratnal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratnal "Ratnal").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-34)

In [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad"), 1,021 apartments and 82 houses collapsed, and 752 people were killed.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-NIDM-19) Collapsing multistory buildings also caused deaths in [Morbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morbi "Morbi") and [Surat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surat "Surat").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-sudhirjain-15) The [Indian military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Armed_Forces "Indian Armed Forces") provided emergency support which was later augmented by the [International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_Red_Cross_and_Red_Crescent_Societies "International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies"). A temporary [Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cross "Red Cross") hospital remained in Bhuj to provide care while a replacement hospital was built.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-35)

There were also 19 deaths in [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-36) The [Badin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badin_District "Badin District")-[Tharparkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tharparkar "Tharparkar") area recorded 12 deaths, 115 injuries, 1,989 collapsed homes and 43,643 damaged homes.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-37) Liquefaction from the earthquake resulted in [sugarcane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarcane "Sugarcane") farms being flooded, affecting crops in the village of Kadhan.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-geer-30)

## Reconstruction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Reconstruction")]

Four months after the earthquake the [Gujarat government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Gujarat "Government of Gujarat") announced the Gujarat Earthquake Reconstruction and Rehabilitation Policy. The policy proposed a different approach to urban and rural construction with the estimated cost of rebuilding to be US$1.77 billion.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:0-38)

The main objectives of the policy included repairing, building, and strengthening houses and public buildings. Other objectives included the revival of the economy, health support, and reconstruction of the community and social infrastructure.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:0-38)

### Housing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Housing")]

The housing policies focused on the removal of rubble, setting up temporary shelters, full reconstruction of damaged houses, and the [retrofitting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retrofitting "Retrofitting") of undamaged units. The policy established a community-driven housing recovery process. The communities affected by the earthquake were given the option for complete or partial relocation to [in-situ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_situ "In situ") reconstruction.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-39) The total number of eligible houses to be repaired was 929,682 and the total number of eligible houses to be reconstructed was 213,685. By 2003, 882,896 (94%) houses were repaired and 113,271 (53%) were reconstructed.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:2-40)

### City planning

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: City planning")]

The Environmental Planning Collaborative (EPC) was commissioned to provide a new city plan for the city of [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:1-41) The plan focused on creating a wider roadway network to provide emergency access to the city. The EPC used land readjustment (LR) in the form of eight town planning schemes.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:1-41) This was implemented by deducting land from private lot sizes to create adequate public land for the widening of roadways.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-42) The remaining land was readjusted and given back to the original owners as final plots.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-:1-41)

## Memorials

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2001_Gujarat_earthquake&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Memorials")]

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Smritivan_2001_Gujarat_earthquake_memorial_garden_in_Bhuj%2C_Gujarat%2C_India.jpg/250px-Smritivan_2001_Gujarat_earthquake_memorial_garden_in_Bhuj%2C_Gujarat%2C_India.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Smritivan_2001_Gujarat_earthquake_memorial_garden_in_Bhuj,_Gujarat,_India.jpg)

Smritivan

[Smritivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smritivan_Earthquake_Memorial_and_Museum "Smritivan Earthquake Memorial and Museum"), a memorial park and museum dedicated to victims of the earthquake was built on top of [Bhujia Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhujia_Hill "Bhujia Hill") in [Bhuj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhuj "Bhuj"), [Kutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutch_district "Kutch district") and opened in 2022. Spread over an area of 470 acres, it has more than 13,805 trees, each dedicated to a victim, planted in the garden and 108 small water reservoirs created on the hill.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-Ray-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-46)

[Veer Balak Smarak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veer_Balak_Smarak "Veer Balak Smarak") in [Anjar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anjar,_Gujarat "Anjar, Gujarat") is a memorial dedicated to 185 school children and 20 teachers who died during the earthquake.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-ht1-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-etv-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake#cite_note-49)
